"""Regression coverage: the reader and the writer must agree on which
BEGIN..END pair in a body is the authoritative metadata block.

A task description can quote the block format as an example. If that quote is
unfinished (a BEGIN with no matching END of its own), it must never be mistaken
for the real block — whether it sits before or after it.
"""

import unittest

from registry.model import (
    METADATA_BEGIN,
    METADATA_END,
    Task,
    parse_metadata_block,
    upsert_metadata_block,
)

REAL_TASK = Task(id="real-task", title="Real task", parent=None)


def real_block(task_id="real-task", parent=None, depends_on=()):
    task = Task(id=task_id, title="Real task", parent=parent, depends_on=depends_on)
    return upsert_metadata_block("", task).strip()


class ParseMetadataBlockTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_no_block_returns_empty(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_metadata_block(""), {})
        self.assertEqual(parse_metadata_block("just some prose"), {})

    def test_single_complete_block(self):
        body = f"Some notes.\n\n{real_block(parent='epic.roots')}\n\nMore notes."
        meta = parse_metadata_block(body)
        self.assertEqual(meta["task-id"], "real-task")
        self.assertEqual(meta["parent"], "epic.roots")

    def test_unfinished_example_before_real_block_is_ignored(self):
        quoted_example = f"{METADATA_BEGIN}\nparent: example.fake\ntask-id: fake-id"
        body = (
            "Format example (do not fill in the end marker below):\n\n"
            f"{quoted_example}\n\n"
            "Actual task:\n\n"
            f"{real_block(parent='epic.roots')}\n"
        )
        meta = parse_metadata_block(body)
        self.assertEqual(meta["task-id"], "real-task")
        self.assertEqual(meta["parent"], "epic.roots")

Confirmed clean — 9/9 tests pass on the fixed code.

## Summary

The bug was in `registry/model.py`'s `parse_metadata_block` (the shared reader): it split on the **first** `<!-- task-registry:begin -->` and the first `END` after it, while `upsert_metadata_block`/`_metadata_bounds` (the writer) picks the **last well-formed pair**, searching backwards to skip any incomplete/stray marker. That disagreement let a quoted, unfinished example block in a task's description leak fields (parent, depends-on, even task-id) into the parsed result, whether the stray marker sat before or after the real block.

Fix: `parse_metadata_block` now calls the same `_metadata_bounds` the writer uses, and returns `{}` when there's no complete pair — no separate parsing logic to keep in sync.

I checked the two sibling consumers (`registry/providers/local.py` and `registry/providers/github.py`); both go through `parse_metadata_block`/`task_from_metadata`, so the fix covers both without further changes. `local.py`'s `_unmanaged_regions` (used for write-time text preservation, not field parsing) was left untouched since it's outside this bug's scope.

Added `tests/test_metadata_block.py` (stdlib `unittest`, no new deps) covering: no block, a single complete block, unfinished examples before/after the real block, an unfinished-only body, reader/writer agreement after `upsert_metadata_block`, preserved surrounding human text, and preserved comma-containing/repeated evidence/reproduction/proposed-fix entries. Verified the new tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after the fix.

Nothing was committed or pushed, per your instructions.
